doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Joining the Messengers and moving to New York
title: Blakey's telegram, leaving for New York, and the Washington engagement
summary: Bobby Paine delivers a telegram from Art Blakey; Ware flies to New York and joins the Messengers in Washington wearing a borrowed short suit.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Anyway, they told me -- I was away somewhere, I was hanging out on 43rd Street and word got to me that Bobby Paine wanted to see me, so I went out to the Cotton Club, and he said, "Man, this is a telegram and Art Blakey wants you to come to New York." I said, "Oh my God." I didn't want to leave Chicago because I was afraid to go to New York, actually, you know, although I really didn't have nothing in Chicago to hold me there.

So I was talking to Paul about it and he said, "Man, you're going to New York, man -- that's where you need to be." And he hung out with me all that night, and we partied, you know, and what have you -- and took me to the plane the next morning -- a bunch of fellows. I had a shopping bag, a suit somebody give me, a couple of shirts, and that was it.

I threw my outfit away because I contacted him and he said to go to this house when you get in town -- his sister in law's house, and he gives me a pep talk, and he had jobs lined up for me all the way to the West Coast, and we wasn't
gonna -- none of us were gonna use any drugs at all, and blah, blah, blah. Sure.

Anyway, I get to New York and Paul told me in the train station, 'Look, man -- we got a place out in East New York' - they had a little inn out there or something like that -- and he said, 'you can stay out there until you get on your feet', you know; And, because I was trying to find all kinds of excuses not to leave Chicago.

And he said, 'No, man, you need to be in New York.' (Unintelligible). Anyway, I get on the plane to New York, and they had a one nighter down in Washington, D.C. They made it. They had Kenny Drew, Donald Bird, Ira Arnie Sullivan, and I forgot -- he used some bass player down in Washington in my place, but they came back the next morning, and our next engagement would be Washington for a week, and that's where I made it, and still, instead of my buying a suit, he said, 'Well, look, I got a suit', you know; I didn't have a black suit -- and everybody was wearing black suits, and I'm not too tall now, but I'm a little taller than he was, so I had to wear the pants -- the coat wasn't too bad, but the pants was real short on me, you know, and I felt just like sliding off of the bandstand -- when we were finished, oh boy, I acted like I was really in to the music, I didn't pay no attention to that too much, though.
